title: Microburst reserve pricing & HC playbook (Aug 2026)
content:
Objective:
This is a tactical playbook for pricing sensitivity and headcount actions specifically tailored to 'microburst' usage patterns — short, repeated spikes in token velocity that materially change unit economics over weekly windows. The goal is to define observable triggers, cost models, and an executable headcount + reserve-capacity response that preserves margin while keeping product SLAs.

Context and why this is different:
- Existing pricing/hc analyses assume steady-state throughput or long-tail seasonal changes. Microbursts (10–90 minute spikes repeated multiple times per day) change two levers: instantaneous reserved capacity need and average utilization. 
- For customers using bursty features (realtime assistants, interactive code generation, live summarization), small changes in pricing or commit can swing margin. This doc builds microburst-forward scenarios and HC triggers for finance and ops to act quickly.

Key metrics and signals (primary observables):
- 5m token-velocity: tokens/sec for rolling 5-minute windows (primary microburst detector)
- Peak-to-median ratio (P/M): ratio of 95th percentile 5m velocity to median 5m velocity over a 7-day window
- Reserve utilization ratio (RUR): reserved capacity used during bursts (% of reserved pool consumed at 95th pct burst)
- Unit cost delta (UCD): estimated change in $/1k tokens between baseline and burst-handling strategy
- SLA tail latency breach rate: % of requests > 300ms tail during bursts

Assumptions (back-of-envelope, adjustable):
- Baseline per-million-token cost (hosted, mixed model) = $1.90 / 1M tokens (includes infra + model licensing + overhead)
- Reserved pool hourly amortized cost for a mid-tier GPU slot = $2.20 / hour equivalent per 1M tokens of expected monthly throughput (this is a modeling simplification)
- Burst premium (on-demand fallback cost) = 1.9x baseline per-token in worst-case (e.g., cross-region fallback + preemptible fill)
- Effective additional SRE/SE ops for high-churn customers = 0.05 FTE per large-customer cohort, or ~$6k/mo in contractor spend when active

Mini cost model (how to compute UCD quickly):
- Inputs: median_tokens_week, peak95_tokens_week, reserved_commit (M tokens/day equivalent), on_demand_fraction_during_burst
- Baseline_cost = median_tokens_week * baseline_perM / 1M
- Burst_cost = (peak95_tokens_week - reserved_commit) * baseline_perM * burst_premium / 1M
- Reserved_cost = reserved_commit * reserved_hourly_amort * 24 * 7 / 1M (weekly amortized)
- UCD = (Baseline_cost + Burst_cost + Reserved_cost) / total_tokens_week - baseline_perM/1M

Three microburst scenarios (numbers are illustrative):
1) Frictional microbursts (low magnitude, frequent):
   - Median weekly tokens: 120M, Peak95 weekly tokens: 180M (P/M=1.5)
   - Proposed reserved_commit: 30M/day equivalent (210M/week) => covers most bursts, RUR ~85%
   - Staff friction: +0.02 FTE ops active
   - Expected unit cost delta: +6% vs baseline (due to reserved amortization)
   - Suggested actions: small reserved slab, no pricing change, auto-batched ingress tuning, optional short-term contractor for first 60d to stabilize.

2) Episodic large microbursts (high magnitude, predictable times):
   - Median weekly tokens: 60M, Peak95 weekly tokens: 220M (P/M~3.7)
   - Proposed reserved_commit: 60M/day (420M/week) -> covers bursts with headroom, RUR ~52%
   - Staff friction: +0.10 FTE for customer success/RAM during on-boarding and first two weeks of each campaign
   - Expected unit cost delta: -2% vs baseline if reserved is sold as a discount tier to customer (customer commit subsidizes cost), otherwise +22% if Redwood absorbs reserved amortization without price pass-through
   - Suggested actions: offer a short-term burst-commit SKU (30-day commit) at a modest discount, require telemetry tags for burst windows, conditional contractor standby.

3) Unbounded microbursts (unpredictable and large):
   - Median weekly tokens: 40M, Peak95 weekly tokens: 520M (P/M~13)
   - Reserved_commit: conservative 50M/day (350M/week) -> RUR ~150% when bursts hit (i.e., reserved inadequate)
   - Staff friction: +0.25 FTE across SRE + solutions engineering during incidence windows; need to trigger cross-region spill policies frequently
   - Expected unit cost delta: +45% if using on-demand fallback regularly; margin erosion unless prices change or guaranteed commit secured
   - Suggested actions: require risk sharing (higher price-per-token for burst tail), implement automatic throttling and user-visible rate-limits, convert high-burst customers to dedicated/dedicated-burst SKU or require short-term commit and pass-through of reserved costs.

Playbook: observable -> recommended finance/ops action (escalation ladder)
- Trigger A (P/M > 2.0 AND 5m token-velocity spike sustaining > 10 min): ops-alert -> activate temporary burst routing (fallback to cheaper quantized model), notify account team, estimate hourly reserve gap and run 'deploy temporary slab' flow. Finance: compute immediate UCD and produce 'one-off surcharge' estimate for AM to discuss with customer.
- Trigger B (RUR > 120% during repeated bursts on 3 separate days in a rolling 7-day window): cross-functional review (finance, product, customer success) within 48 hours. Options to present: incremental short-term commit, temporary surcharge, convert to Dedicated trial.
- Trigger C (SLA tail breach rate > 1% in burst windows OR customer complaints for latency): immediate mitigation prioritized over margin (apply throttles, fallback). Post-incident: formal margin review and recommended re-pricing within 14 days.

Headcount and contractor playbook (fast actions):
- Low friction events (Trigger A): redeploy existing on-call SRE rotation, authorize up to 0.05 FTE contractor ops for 30 days without exec approval.
- Medium friction (Trigger B): authorize hiring pool release for 0.1–0.2 FTE contractor for 90 days; product/solutions engineering shadowed for onboarding; finance snapshots for cost-pass decisions.
- High friction (Trigger C / repeated unbounded bursts): recommend immediate temporary hire of 0.25 FTE SRE + 0.25 FTE solutions (2 contractors) for up to 180 days; escalate to VP finance for headcount reclassification if sustained beyond 60 days.

Pricing levers (experiment matrix):
- Short-term burst surcharge: +20–40% on per-token price for tokens above customer’s baseline committed 95th pct. Pros: immediate margin protection. Cons: customer friction.
- Time-of-day premium: premium for off-peak vs peak windows. Useful for scheduled, predictable bursts.
- Short-term commit SKU: 7/30-day slab that offers discount vs on-demand but requires a minimum commit; automates reserved amortization pass-through.
- QoS-tiered model pricing: different model families or quantization profiles priced lower for burst coverage.

Experiment design (A/B brief):
- Objective: measure elasticity of burst-origin customers to a 25% short-term surcharge on tail tokens.
- Population: top 12 customers by burst P/M in last 30 days (with opt-in/consent as needed).
- Metrics: churn risk (customer-initiated support tickets), change in burst velocity, revenue delta, margin delta.
- Duration: 30 days with weekly check-ins; if churn risk > 8% escalate to GTM.

Reporting & weekly cadence items for finance/ops:
- Weekly microburst ledger: list customers hitting triggers, estimated incremental cost (UCD) and proposed collection action
- Monthly retrospective: compare predicted vs realized UCD, contractor spend, SLAs. Feed into pricing model and adjust reserved amortization assumptions.

Quick-reference decision table (summary):
- P/M < 1.8, RUR < 100% -> operational tune, no pricing action required.
- 1.8 <= P/M < 3.0, RUR 100–140% -> offer 30-day burst commit SKU OR small surcharge; authorize 0.05–0.1 FTE contractor.
- P/M >= 3.0 OR RUR > 140% -> require dedicated conversation: recommend dedicated/dedicated-burst SKU, reprice tail tokens, authorize up to 0.25 FTE contractors for 90–180 days.

Quick templates (snippets for AMs / finance to use in outreach):
- Short pitch for 30-day burst commit: "We see repeating short bursts that materially increase the marginal cost of serving your workload. A 30-day burst-commit at a modest discount lets us provision reserved capacity to guarantee your latency and reduce your effective per-token price for the campaign duration."
- One-off surcharge justification note: "Observed 95th pct burst exceeded committed capacity in 48% of windows over last 7 days, increasing on-demand fallbacks and unit cost. Proposed temporary surcharge applies to tokens above your baseline 95th percentile for the next 30 days while we provision a dedicated slab."

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Finance: build a weekly UCD dashboard (owner: Marco) — ETA 2 weeks.
- Product: instrument 5m token-velocity and P/M alerting in the console (owner: Lena) — ETA 3 weeks.
- Ops: draft step-by-step temporary slab deployment runbook (owner: Owen) — ETA 10 business days.
- GTM/AM: finalize short-form sku language + customer outreach templates (owner: Asha) — ETA 7 business days.

Appendix: quick worked example (conservative numbers):
- median_week=100M, peak95=250M, reserved_commit=210M/week equivalent
- Baseline_cost = 100 * $1.90 = $190
- Burst_cost = max(0, 250-210)*1.9*1.90 = 40 * 1.9 * 1.90 = $140.6
- Reserved_cost weekly amort (approx) = 210 * $2.20 * 24*7 / 1M ~ simplification -> treat as $210 * 0.037 = $7.77 (note: this amort model intentionally conservative for quick calc)
- Total_weekly = 190 + 140.6 + 7.77 = $338.37 -> effective $/M = $3.3837 -> delta vs baseline ~ +78%.
- Interpretation: this customer is a primary candidate for commit or surcharge.

Notes and open questions:
- Validate reserved amort assumptions with infra finance (the hourly amortization proxy is a simplification; need per-GPU SKU amort curves).
- Consider creating a short-lived burst-trial contract template for legal to speed up conversion.
- Need to track CMGR of burst customers separately in finance reporting (they bias consumption and cost forecasts).

End of playbook.
